subject: Biotechnology
title: Clopidogrel and CYP2C19
description: A 60-second lesson on Clopidogrel and CYP2C19.

hook.text: Clopidogrel prevents heart attacks — but one in three patients cannot activate it. Their CYP2C19 gene is the reason.

buildup.text: Clopidogrel is a prodrug requiring CYP2C19 activation — loss-of-function variants leave the drug inactive.

discovery.text: Poor metabolizers have 40% higher risk of stent thrombosis — the drug meant to protect them does not work.

twist.text: Alternative drugs like ticagrelor do not need CYP2C19 activation — but they cost more and cause more bleeding.

climax.text: Preemptive pharmacogenomic testing at Mount Sinai saves $1,500 per patient by avoiding ineffective clopidogrel prescriptions.

punchline.text: Test the gene, choose the drug — CYP2C19 testing saves hearts and money.

quiz.question: Why doesn't clopidogrel work in some patients?
options: Their blood is naturally resistant to all anti-clotting drugs
CYP2C19 loss-of-function variants prevent activation of the prodrug into its active form
Their stents are made of a material that blocks clopidogrel absorption

details.summary: Clopidogrel is a blood thinner requiring activation by the CYP2C19 liver enzyme. About 30 percent of people carry genetic variants making this enzyme less active, reducing clopidogrel effectiveness and increasing heart attack risk.
details.whyItMatters: Millions of patients receive clopidogrel after heart procedures. Those with poor CYP2C19 metabolism have significantly higher rates of stent thrombosis and heart attacks.
takeaways: CYP2C19 poor metabolizers cannot activate clopidogrel effectively
About 30 percent of patients carry reduced-function CYP2C19 variants
Pharmacogenomic testing enables selection of alternative antiplatelet drugs

faq.question: How common is CYP2C19 poor metabolism?
faq.answer: Approximately 2 to 5 percent of Europeans and 15 to 20 percent of East Asians are poor metabolizers with two non-functional alleles. An additional 25 to 35 percent are intermediate metabolizers with one non-functional allele. Together, roughly one-third of patients may not respond optimally.

faq.question: What alternative drugs are prescribed for CYP2C19 poor metabolizers?
faq.answer: Prasugrel and ticagrelor do not require CYP2C19 activation and provide effective antiplatelet activity regardless of genotype. FDA labeling for clopidogrel now includes pharmacogenomic information recommending alternatives for poor metabolizers, though testing is not yet universally implemented.
